newsitem.title: PANAMA: U.N. condemns Panama's repatriation of Colombians.
newsitem.headline: U.N. condemns Panama's repatriation of Colombians.

text.p: The United Nations refugee agency said on Monday it opposed Panama's decision to repatriate Colombian refugees.
"The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) is against the repatriation because we can't confirm that they were repatriated voluntarily," regional deputy head Flor Rojas told Reuters.

Interior Minister Raul Montenegro maintained that Panama had not violated any international human rights accords by reaching an agreement with Colombia over the weekend to repatriate nearly 300 Colombians, mostly women and children, to Bahia Cupica, a tourist area on Colombia's Pacific coast.
"Panama has complied with our international accords. We have respected human rights and international solidarity," he told a news conference.
The refugees had fled several weeks ago from violence between guerrilla groups and right-wing death squads in Colombia's northwest region of Uraba along Panama's border.
"International accords establish criteria of voluntary repatriation with conditions of security and dignity. We cannot ensure these occurred," Rojas said.
She said the UNHCR was not invited to see all the sites where the refugees had sought shelter.
However, Montenegro said poor climate and difficult terrain prevented the government from bringing U.N. officials and human rights groups to see all the areas.
"The international organisations are welcome to travel to Colombia to verify that they (the refugees) left the country voluntarily," he said.
